issues.legal_issue: In a proceeding to release requisitioned property, possession is ordinarily to be returned to the person from whom it was taken, and the release inquiry does not determine claims based on facts preceding requisition.
material_facts: The requisition orders were addressed to the appellants as the persons in possession, and possession was taken from them.
Before requisition, their allotments had been provisional and cancellation had been communicated, but the department had not recovered possession.
No subsequent event creating a competing claim to possession was identified; the release orders instead specified the Director of Industries as the recipient.
issues.conclusion: The release inquiry under section 35(1) is required only when facts or events arising after requisition make it necessary. Otherwise, possession should be released to the person from whom it was taken; the government is not to investigate antecedent title in that inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 29(2) and 35(1) of the Defence of India Act, 1962, provide for requisition by an order addressed to the owner or person in possession and for specifying the recipient of possession on release. Section 35(1) permits an inquiry when necessary, including a summary and prima facie inquiry where post-requisition events create a dispute. It does not enlarge the government's authority to adjudicate competing claims based on facts anterior to requisition. Under section 35(2), delivery does not prejudice another person's rights enforceable through due process of law. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.requisition_release_proceeding: The matter concerns release of property that had been requisitioned.
predicates.possession_taken_from_person: The government took possession of the property from a person in possession when it requisitioned the property.
predicates.claim_based_only_on_pre_requisition_fact: The competing claim to possession rests on facts that existed before requisition, with no later event necessitating an inquiry into who should receive possession.
predicates.possession_returned_to_person_from_whom_: Possession is released to the person from whom it was taken at requisition.

issues.definition: When a release proceeding concerns property taken from a person and the competing claim rests only on pre-requisition facts, possession is returned to that person.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose provisional allotment had not become final could receive a conditional order for return of possession where the government had not recovered possession before requisition and no third party had subsequently been allotted the property.
material_facts: The appellant had been given possession under a provisional allotment that was subject to final government approval, and the allotment was later cancelled.
The department had not recovered possession before requisition, and the requisitioning authority took possession from the appellant.
After release from requisition, possession was specified to be given to the department, but the plot had not been allotted to a third party.
The Supreme Court considered that the special-leave appeal warranted a qualified rather than an unconditional order.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed in part: possession was directed to be delivered to the appellant unless the government took adequate and lawful steps to recover formal possession within the specified period. The government remained able to recover possession later, and an aggrieved party could pursue the statutory process for adjudication of rights.
issues.legal_principle: Applying sections 29 and 35 of the Defence of India Act, 1962, the Court held that possession should technically have been released to the person from whom it had been taken. In exercising its jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution, it made relief conditional in light of the provisional nature of the allotment and the fact that the government had not recovered possession before requisition. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_derequisition_order and possession_taken_from_appellant and provisional_allotment_only and government_had_not_recovered_possession_before_requisition and not third_party_allotment_after_release

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_derequisition_: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal challenging an order specifying who should receive possession when requisitioned property was released.
predicates.possession_taken_from_appellant: The requisitioning authority took possession of the property from the appellant.
predicates.provisional_allotment_only: The appellant had received possession under an allotment that remained provisional and subject to final approval.
predicates.government_had_not_recovered_possession_: The government had not taken back possession from the appellant before the property was requisitioned.
predicates.third_party_allotment_after_release: After release from requisition, the property was allotted to a third party.
predicates.conditional_possession_return_order: The court conditionally directs return of possession to the appellant while leaving the government able to recover possession by lawful steps.

issues.definition: Where the appeal concerns release of property taken from a person with only a provisional allotment, the government had not recovered possession before requisition, and no third party received a later allotment, the court may conditionally direct return of possession.

issues.legal_issue: A later allotment of released property to a third party may justify refusing to direct the government to recover possession and dispossess that allottee.
material_facts: The appellant had possessed the plot under a provisional allotment before it was requisitioned.
After the property was released from requisition and possession was given to the Industries department, the department allotted the plot to a third party.
The appellant challenged the release order in a special-leave appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Court dismissed the appeal and declined to direct the government to complete the formal recovery of possession or dispossess the third-party allottee.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the interpretation of sections 29 and 35 of the Defence of India Act, 1962, but concluded on the special facts that it was not just and expedient to direct recovery of possession from the third-party allottee. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_derequisition_order and possession_taken_from_appellant and third_party_allotment_after_release and possession_delivered_to_department

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_derequisition_: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal challenging an order specifying who should receive possession when requisitioned property was released.
predicates.possession_taken_from_appellant: The requisitioning authority took possession of the property from the appellant.
predicates.third_party_allotment_after_release: After release from requisition, the property was allotted to a third party.
predicates.possession_delivered_to_department: Possession of the released property was delivered to a government department.
predicates.appeal_dismissed_without_direction_to_di: The court dismisses the appeal without directing the government to recover possession from or dispossess the third-party allottee.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal challenges release of property taken from the appellant, and the released property has been delivered to a government department and allotted to a third party, the appeal may be dismissed without an order to dispossess that allottee.
